newsitem.title: UK: Cook sees UK getting good EU deal at Amsterdam.
newsitem.headline: Cook sees UK getting good EU deal at Amsterdam.

text.p: Britain is poised to secure a good deal at next week's Amsterdam summit to conclude a new European Union treaty thanks to the constructive stance taken by the Labour government, Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said on Monday.
He told parliament he was confident of agreement on four issues of importance for Britain:
-- securing a legal basis -- which could not be challenged in the European Court of Justice -- for Britain to keep control of its external borders.
-- measures that will provide for tougher provisions against fraud in other EU member states.
-- a reweighting of votes in the council of ministers to give a louder voice to the bloc's four big countries.
Together these have a majority of the EU population but, in an enlarged EU, they might not have a blocking minority under current weightings, Cook said.
"We can look forward with confidence to obtaining more votes for Britain and the larger countries out of the Amsterdam summit," he said.
-- retaining the national veto in foreign and security policy.
"We can return from Amsterdam not just having done a good deal for Britain but having obtained a better deal for Britain that the previous government could have hoped to achieve," Cook said.

He said the Labour government had already re-established Britain as a leading player in Europe because, unlike former prime minister John Major's administration, it was no longer heckling from the sidelines.

"Precisely because this government is not shouting 'No' to everything out of prejudice, that we are listened to with respect when we do say 'No' to issues that threaten Britain's national interests," the Foreign Secretary said.
